core.title: Write the main job in JTBD grammar and derived outcome statements in ODI grammar
core.given: You are decomposing work into a main job statement and its derived outcome statements (the outcome-level plan artifacts) in plan artifacts
core.when: you write the main job statement or a derived outcome statement
core.then: State the main job in JTBD job-statement grammar (verb + object + contextual clarifier) and each derived outcome statement in ODI outcome grammar (direction + dimension + object_of_control + context_clarifier), keeping the two grammars separate.
prefer: Main job as a JTBD statement: verb + object + contextual clarifier.
Derived outcome statements as ODI outcomes filling all four ODI fields: direction + dimension + object_of_control + context_clarifier.
avoid: Premature collapse: stating the main job as an outcome too early (replacing the job statement with an ODI outcome statement).
Mixing the grammars: writing derived outcome statements as job statements instead of ODI outcomes.
core.why: Collapsing the job into an outcome too early produces malformed plan artifacts, so the two grammars must stay separate.
evidence: The main job statement is structured as verb + object + contextual clarifier and is not substituted by an ODI outcome statement (direction + dimension + object_of_control + context_clarifier).
Each derived outcome statement populates the four ODI fields: direction, dimension, object_of_control and context_clarifier.
verification: Term definitions for the check: a JTBD job statement is verb + object + contextual clarifier; an ODI outcome is direction + dimension + object_of_control + context_clarifier.

Premature collapse — stating the main job as an outcome too early, i.e. replacing the job statement with an ODI outcome statement — is what the check forbids, because it yields malformed plan artifacts.
Whether a main job statement has been substituted by an ODI outcome statement requires language judgement (llm_judged); it is not mechanically decidable in general.
Missing ODI fields in a derived outcome statement are mechanically checkable against the stack's plan-artifact schema where the stack defines one.

fires: The planner writes the main job statement for a plan artifact
The planner authors or edits derived outcome statements (direction, dimension, object_of_control, context_clarifier)
A main job statement is written as an ODI outcome statement instead of verb + object + contextual clarifier
doesNotFire: Editing plan prose unrelated to the job statement or the derived outcome statements
The coder implements code or tests from an already-decomposed plan
Acceptance-criteria wording that is neither the main job nor a derived outcome statement

neutralityNotes: The convention is methodology-level (JTBD job grammar vs ODI outcome grammar) and needed little neutralization: the ATDD-Bun artifact names were replaced — 'DESIRED OUTCOME' by the role-level 'derived outcome statement' (concrete kinds via roles.plan_artifact.kinds), 'plan/' by 'plan artifacts' (root via roots.plan), and the 'desired-outcome.schema' pointers, which are carried in bunOnly. The four ODI component names (direction, dimension, object_of_control, context_clarifier) are kept verbatim in the core because they are the grammar the obligation prescribes, not stack mechanics. The finding ids of the Bun realization, the source term-id labels (jtbd, odi, premature_collapse) and their textbook example stay in bun.json; the core's verification restates the definitions generically and preserves the split between llm_judged collapse detection and mechanical missing-field checking. 'unless' is empty in bun.json and stays empty, so no exception was dropped or added.
